flawed_step: The first required step—deducing that an arbitrary tournament on four vertices contains a directed cycle—is unjustified. A tournament may be transitive and therefore acyclic.
counterexample: Take vertices {1,2,3,4} with arcs 1→2, 1→3, 1→4, 2→3, 2→4, and 3→4. This is a tournament because each pair has exactly one directed arc. Every arc goes from a smaller number to a larger number, so labels strictly increase along any directed path. Consequently no directed cycle exists, and in particular there is no Hamiltonian cycle.
assessment_summary: The statement is false: the explicit transitive tournament on four vertices has no directed cycle at all.
